newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Wessex keen to speed benefits.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Wessex keen to speed benefits.

text.p: British water and sewerage company Wessex Water Plc hopes to announce its plans to return benefits to shareholders "certainly in the next six months," chief executive Colin Skellett told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"I hope it could be a lot quicker than that...we are not going to sit with that ungeared balance sheet," he said.
Wessex announced pre-tax profits for the half year of 75.5 million stg, up 10.4 percent from a year ago, and hiked its dividend 14 percent to 5.7 pence.
It said it was considering options to deliver higher returns to shareholders and Skellett said this covered "a whole range."
Skellett said these included other possibilities for investments, balance sheet restructuring or a combination of moves.
"We want it to be right for shareholders," he said.
He said any potential acquisitions would be "relevant to our business...we are not going to go into anything that we do not understand."
Wessex had its proposed bid to take over fellow water company South West Water blocked by the UK government in October along with a rival plan from Severn Trent.
It now has net cash of 75 million stg on its balance sheet.

Skellett said the company was shedding around 20-30 jobs at senior levels which would then knock-on through the rest of the company as it makes an internal restructuring following the failure of its plans to bid for South West Water.
The company said it expected to maintain the momentum of a four percent decrease in operational expenditure in its water business into the second half.
Skellett said other ways of cost saving came from buying arrangements and integrating service arrangements.
"We are happy to work with anybody as long as it takes costs out," he said.
Skellett said turnover at its UK Waste business was hit to the tune of three million stg in the first half as a result of a sharp drop in waste paper and cardboard prices.
But he added that this appeared to be stopping and that the "underlying business is growing nicely."

The waste management unit which Wessex owns with Waste Management International turned in pre-tax profits of 12.4 million stg of which Wessex took 6.2 million stg. Wessex is also undertaking a survey of customer requirements and Skellett said this should help direct investment.
"We are determined this time to get investment linked to what customers want," he said.
